title: BIOMASS SC Test Facilities
description:
The BIOMASS programme was selected as the 7th Earth Explorer mission in 
Spring 2013 in Graz, Austria. The overall objective of the mission is to 
reduce the uncertainty in the worldwide spatial distribution and dynamics 
of forest biomass in order to improve current assessments and future 
projections of the global carbon cycle.
 
The objective will be achieved by implementation of a P-band SAR mission, 
providing global maps of forest biomass stocks, forest disturbance and 
growth.

This notification of Intended Invitation To Tender concerns the procurement 
of Biomass SC Test Facilities by Airbus Defence and Space Ltd as Prime 
contractor of the Biomass project. The supplier selection will be made in 
accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices.

The scope of this procurement covers the services of a test house to 
perform certain tests required for the SC Test Facilities.

The SC Test Facilities are required to test and qualify the Biomass S/C for 
the mechanical launch environment and in-orbit environment through 
vibration, acoustic, shock, EMC, mass properties and thermal vacuum 
testing, and the instrument PFM for thermal vacuum, RF and EMC testing. The 
test campaigns required to run are Instrument PFM, SM test campaign and PFM 
campaign

In this framework, the present Invitation To Tender will be addressed to 
economic operators (including those deemed to act as subcontractors) whose 
registered office is established in such Member and Associated States 
which, by the time of the Contract award decision, will be a participating 
State in the ESA Biomass project. 

The following States are participating in the said Programme: Austria,
Belgium, Canada, Czech Republic, Denmark, Finland, France, Germany,
Ireland, Italy, Luxembourg, The Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, 
Romania, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland and the United Kingdom.

description:
The CNES hereby informs you that the activities detailed below will be subject to a European tender procedure with publication on ESA-STAR in the coming months:
Context:
The CNES wishes to renovate the Space Museum in Kourou, French Guiana, to make it a space adapted to the expectations of its target public. This renovation encompasses all the interior spaces (permanent exhibition, reception area, shop), as well as the building’s cladding and the addition of exterior facilities.
Reflection on the renovation of the Space Museum is part of the strategy to promote in French Guiana the image of space and of the Guiana Space Centre (CSG), Europe’s Spaceport.
The design of the project is global and focuses on attractiveness in order to enhance the visit experience for all visitors: families, school groups, customers, institutions, employees, service providers, and others.
In addition, the project is part of a broader context, in particular associated with:
-	The modernisation of the image of the Guiana Space Centre (CSG),
-	The improvement of a global tourism offer of the CSG and the expectations regarding the welcoming of visitors,
-	A strong demand for information about the CSG and space activity in French Guiana.

Purpose of the contract:
This information concerns the contracts for works related to museum displays, scenography and graphic aspects.
The work for the CNES/CSG, at the site of the Space Museum at the Guiana Space Centre in Kourou (French Guiana), falls within a demanding operational context (project integrating an architectural and a scenographic component, CSG environment, location), which the contractor will need to take into account in their bid.
Please note that the renovation project is also the subject of a BIM-GEM (Building Information Modelling - Management-Operation-Maintenance) strategy from the design stage through to the use of the structure.

title: Biomass Propulsion Subsystem
description:
The BIOMASS programme was selected as the 7th Earth Explorer mission in
Spring 2013 at the User Consultation Meeting in Graz, Austria. The overall
objective of the mission is to reduce the uncertainty in the worldwide
spatial distribution and dynamics of forest biomass in order to improve 
current assessments and future projections of the global carbon cycle. 

The objective will be achieved by implementation of a P-band SAR mission,
providing global maps of forest biomass stocks, forest disturbance and 
growth.

This notification of Intended Invitation To Tender concerns the procurement 
of Biomass Satellite Reaction Control System (RCS) / Propulsion Subsystem 
by Airbus Defence and Space Ltd as Prime contractor of the Biomass project.
The supplier selection will be made in accordance with the principles of 
ESA Best Practices.

The scope of this procurement covers the design, development (including the 
required delta-qualification activities if any), manufacturing, testing and 
delivery of the Satellite Propulsion Subsystem.

The Propulsion Subsystem function is to perform Orbital Control Manoeuvres 
throughout the whole mission, including disposal, and to enhance the 
Attitude Control capabilities during Acquisition and Safe Hold phases.

It consists of the following major elements / design features:

 - A pressure driven design with the tank ullage pressurised to 22 bar 
at launch (BOL) and reducing to 5.5 bar at propellant depletion (EOL). 
- Two fully independent thruster branches, each with four 1 N 
straight nozzle thrusters, isolated by a dedicated latch valve guaranteeing 
operational robustness. 
- Fill and drain/vent valves incorporate a number of independent 
mechanical barriers to on-ground leakage to support compliance to the CSG 
Launch Site Safety Requirements.
- Pressure monitoring is provided by pressures transducers, the two 
thruster branch transducers being available for flight and an additional 
propellant

title: Messsystem Verformung Ganzblattprüfung - PR434295-3350-W
description: 1 Stück Messsystem Verformung Ganzblattprüfung Das 3d-Messsystem soll im Bereich "Ganzblattprüfung" des Fraunhofer IWES zur Messung der Verformungen bzw. Positionen von Messpunkten an einem Rotorblatt während eines Tests dienen. Ziel sind die Punktkoordinaten in unserem Prüfstands-Koordinatensystem. Dabei ist das Rotorblatt im Freien montiert, hat eine Länge von ca. 115m bei einer Höhe der Messpunkte von bis zu Größenordnung 50m über Grund. Aufgrund der stark unterschiedlichen Lichtverhältnisse und Störeinflüsse wie Regen und Nebel schließen wir ein optisches Messverfahren aus, so dass sich Satellitennavigation (GNSS) anbietet. Das System muss komplett wetterfest sein und sowohl im Winter als auch im Sommer arbeiten können. Es sollen 10 Messpunkte (optional mehr) mit mindestens 10 Hz Abtastrate und einer Genauigkeit von mindestens 5cm oder besser gemessen werden. Der Anbieter soll die Einbindung der Echtzeit-Messdaten in unser vorhandenes HMB-MGC-Messsystem sicherstellen.

title: OPEN REPROGRAMMABLE SPACE INFRASTRUCTURE TESTBED FOR BEYOND 5G (B5G) END-TO-END SOLUTIONS AND SERVICES (ARTES 4.0 SPL 5G/6G 3E.019)
description: The objective of the activity is to develop and test a reprogrammable testbed in space to permit the experimentation of Beyond 5G (B5G) satellite features and capabilities and enable technology verification and demonstration; rapid validation of end-to-end solutions and services, following the principles of continuous development/continuous integration. B5G satellitefeatures will be implemented in the testbed as part of the activity to demonstrate its capabilities.Targeted Improvements:Enabling development infrastructure for B5G satellite systems not existing today.Description:With the establishment of Non-Terrestrial Networks (NTN) firmly as part of 3GPP rel. 17, we are witnessing efforts for the validation of initial designs and deployments of integrated terrestrial (TN) and NTN networks to offer Enhanced Mobile Broadband (eMBB) and Internet-of-Things (IoT) services.Nonetheless, the work to define Beyond 5G (B5G)/towards 6G continues with the roadmap rapidly evolving alongside the 3GPP standardisation process, e.g., NTN enhancements included in rel. 18, advanced NTN features already proposed for Rel. 19 and initial assessments of B5G/towards 6G space infrastructure. However, evaluating the implementation of new architectures is challenging mainly due to immaturity of technology and lack of means for continuous development and validation of new capabilities, which hinders the time to market for NTN solutions.The objective of the activity is then to develop and test a reprogrammable testbed for space infrastructure to permit the experimentation of 5G/6G satellite features and capabilities and enable technology verification and demonstration; rapid validation of end-to-end solutions and services, following the principles of continuous development/ continuous integration. The testbed will implement featuresbased on mid to longer term technology trends such as cross-layer communication, dynamically programmable backhaul, OpenRAN implementations, use of AI/ML onboard, context aware routing and increased importance of security-by-design. Candidate features will be assessed and expected performance, benefits and costs for each will be identified and documented. The activity will implement and demonstrate enhanced NTN features (rel.18/19) in orbit using either transparent or regenerative payloads with onboard storage and computing and routing capabilities and intersatellite links as/if applicable.The testbed could be embarked for example on the ISS, existing/planned smallsats, and/or as hosted payload. The activity will take stock of all ongoing 5G satellite developments and propose convincing demonstrations. The activity will seek synergies with ARTES SPL 5G deliverables and testbeds as well as various European 5Gplatforms and projects and national initiatives that are already being built-up.The activity will be implemented in a phased approach and features will be proposed and implemented by activating CCNs.
